reason: I rank the paired-load experiments first. The supplied probe confirms that SME2 can load two adjacent vectors with each of two instructions, while the incumbent compiler block shows four separate loads. This is code-generation evidence, not proof of a GEMM speedup; several proposals test essentially the same change, so compare their emitted hot loops before selecting a variant. Next, the indirect-store proposals have local correctness and code-generation support plus external motivation, but no hill timing. B-panel packing has a clear locality hypothesis, with packing cost and 64 KiB panel size as risks. The schedule and streaming-region changes are narrower hypotheses without matching probe evidence. Scratch lifetime and row-panel transpose may reduce temporary footprint, but retain transpose work and need full-call timing. I rank transpose fusion last: the proposed schedule still writes and reads full scratch, and ZA is needed for both transpose and four-tile accumulation, so it may add transfers without removing the scratch traffic. No supplied scores establish a gain for any proposal.
